name: Question 18
problem: Estimate $(1.81)\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(0.91)$ using a differential $\text{d}f$ of the function $f(x,y)=x\operatorname{ln}⁡y$ at the point $(2,1).$
worked_solution:
First, let's find the differential:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}f(x,y) & =(\frac{∂f}{∂x})\,\text{d}x+(\frac{∂f}{∂y})\,\text{d}y \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡y\,\text{d}x+\frac{x}{y}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

At the point $(2,1),$ the differential is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}f(x,y) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)\,\text{d}x+\frac{2}{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & =0\,\text{d}x+2\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

So, if we move to the point $(2+Δx,1+Δy),$ then we can approximate the change in $f$ as

$$
Δf≈0\,Δx+2\,Δy
$$

Note that 

$$
(1.81)\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(0.91)=f(1.81,0.91),
$$

so we want to move to the point $(1.81,0.91).$

Moving from $(2,1)$ to $(1.81,0.91),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Δx & =1.81-2=-0.19, \\ Δy & =0.91-1=-0.09.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Δf & ≈0\cdot (-0.19)+2\cdot (-0.09) \\  & ≈0-0.18 \\  & ≈-0.18.\end{aligned}
$$

This means that the value of $f$ decreases by about $0.18.$ Consequently, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1.81,0.91) & ≈f(2,1)-0.18 \\ (1.81)\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(0.91) & ≈2\operatorname{ln}⁡1-0.18 \\  & ≈0-0.18 \\  & ≈-0.18.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

df(x,y)=(∂f∂x)dx+(∂f∂y)dy=ln⁡ydx+xydy.

At the point (2,1), the differential is

df(x,y)=ln⁡(1)dx+21dy=0dx+2dy.

So, if we move to the point (2+Δx,1+Δy), then we can approximate the change in f as

Δf≈0Δx+2Δy

Note that (1.81)⋅ln⁡(0.91)=f(1.81,0.91),

so we want to move to the point (1.81,0.91).

Moving from (2,1) to (1.81,0.91), we have

Δx=1.81−2=−0.19,Δy=0.91−1=−0.09.

So, we have

Δf≈0⋅(−0.19)+2⋅(−0.09)≈0−0.18≈−0.18.

f(1.81,0.91)≈f(2,1)−0.18(1.81)⋅ln⁡(0.91)≈2ln⁡1−0.18≈0−0.18≈−0.18.
